title: Priority-path circuit-breaker to contain token-surge and restore TTFT
creator: Asha Mehta
description: Several enterprise customers reported recurrent first-token latency spikes (TTFT) and tokens/sec collapse during multi-tenant prompt-fanout windows across Hosted and Dedicated. Investigation shows a correlated token surge that overwhelms the fairness queue and triggers aggressive KV prefetch attempts on heterogeneous kernels, causing kernel-selection stalls and a cascading increase in initial-token latency. This ticket implements a lightweight "priority-path" circuit-breaker that isolates high-priority traffic, applies conservative KV-prefetch limits for lower-priority tenants, and short-circuits expensive kernel-selection retries to prevent system-wide TTFT regression.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Replay customer trace captured 2026-03-10 (trace-id: rwd-20260310-5302) with 60% prompt fanout across 3 model variants
2) Use loadtool with rungroup mix matching tenant-priority tags (high:20%, medium:30%, low:50%)
3) Observe tokens/sec drop and TTFT increase > 500ms for medium/low tenants once KV prefetch queue saturation crosses threshold
4) Correlate with kernel-selection logs showing repeated fallback attempts and long scheduling latencies
investigation_notes: Root cause hypothesis: simultaneous token surges from low-priority tenants cause the router to attempt aggressive KV warmup and kernel heuristics, which preempt CPU/GPU resources and block fast-path scheduling for high-priority requests
Heap of evidence: p99 TTFT traces, scheduler histograms, per-model kernel-selection timing, and per-tenant prefetch counters (see dashboard links)
Reproducible in staging with synthetic fanout and an artificial slow kernel backend injected (kernel-latency +40ms)
mitigation_plan: Phase A (short-term, rollout today): Implement circuit-breaker configured at router layer that throttles KV-prefetch for priority<50 and enforces a max of 4 concurrent kernel-selection retries per request
Phase B (next 48h): Add fast-path pinning for high-priority requests that bypass expensive fallback heuristics and get scheduled on reserved worker slots
Phase C (2 weeks): Bake in adaptive thresholds driven by observed queueing latency and add telemetry to detect token-surge precursors for automated gradual shedding
rollback_plan: If the circuit-breaker causes unexpected throughput regressions for Dedicated customers, revert the router flag immediately and re-enable previous prefetch settings; keep the fast-path pinning off until root cause fully validated.
monitoring_playbook: Alert: tokens_per_second_cluster drop > 20% with sustained queue depth > 80%
Dashboard panels to watch: per-tenant TTFT, KV-prefetch concurrency, kernel-selection attempts, worker slot utilization
Rollback triggers: new error increase > 0.5% or sustained TPS drop > 15% after rollout
